title: Articles LXIII–LXVIII · On the fifth species of contemplation — the goods of nature and the consideration of the created universe

blocks.s: [Articles LXIII–LXVIII develop the fifth species of contemplation, consisting in the consideration of the gifts of nature: first the soul's own natural powers and their ordering; then the natural dignity of the human person as made in God's image; then the variety and order of the visible creation — the elements, the living creatures, the heavens and their order — all of which are contemplated not for their own sake but as vestiges and mirrors of the divine wisdom, goodness and power. Denis follows Augustine, Gregory and the tradition in reading the book of nature as a ladder to the Creator, and shows how each natural perfection glimpsed in the creature is a dim reflection of the perfection that is in God without limit, without composition, and without shadow.]
